claims.statement: Water-loss guidance is an internal operational aid rather than coverage authority: coverage decisions must use the policy and attached endorsement in force, and investigation, inspection, mitigation authorization, or payment does not by itself waive policy rights or accept the full claim (H.0.1-H.0.2, H.0.11, H.6.7, H.7.3, H.7.6-H.7.8).

The water-loss intake workflow opens a distinct claim file, records source, affected locations, discovery date, and reporter, confirms policy and identity details, acknowledges receipt, communicates investigation status, instructs mitigation within three days after discovery, and issues a reservation of rights within ten days after identifying facts that may limit or preclude coverage when a final decision is not yet supportable (H.6.1-H.6.10).

Notice timing is contract-specific rather than a universal 30-day rule: HO 04 90 requires notice within 30 days after discovery, HO 04 27 and DP 04 95 require notice within 30 days after loss, while the HO-3 2024-03 base form requires prompt notice with the insured, location, and available circumstances.

A water-loss investigation must independently establish source, water path, duration or recurrence, and the connection between the event and direct physical damage; prior loss alone does not establish that current damage is excluded, and conflicting or incomplete causation evidence must be documented and referred when material (H.5.1-H.5.8, H.5.17, H.5.37-H.5.40, H.6.12-H.6.19).

The HO-3 2024-03 base form covers direct physical loss from accidental discharge or overflow of listed plumbing, heating, air-conditioning, sprinkler, or household-appliance systems, but excludes continuous or repeated seepage and does not cover loss to the system or appliance from which water escaped; its water-backup and sump exclusions remain unless an applicable endorsement changes them (P.9, P.29-P.33, X.8-X.9).

HO 04 90 W.1 writes back HO-3 P.9 and X.8-X.9 for water backup and sump discharge or overflow, including sudden or gradual covered water events, while preserving flood, surface-water, maintenance, failed-equipment, and other stated exclusions; HO 04 27 instead covers specified accidental water damage but excludes sewer, drain, and sump backup; DP 04 95 supplies its own water-backup and sump-overflow grant and conditions.

For covered water-backup losses, HO 04 90 (2027-01) applies a single $10,000 limit across covered loss and expenses arising from the same water event and a $1,000 deductible applied to covered damage from the same occurrence; DP 04 95 (2021-05) applies a $5,000 aggregate water-backup limit and a $1,000 deductible applied once to the same covered loss.

HO 04 27 (2016-05) applies a $2,500 limit to sewer or drain backup and sump overflow and a $5,000 limit to fungi, wet or dry rot, or bacteria; those limits apply regardless of claimants, locations, items, or causes and are not combined, with the applicable policy deductible applied to the covered loss.

The claim scope must separate covered direct physical damage, reasonable emergency mitigation, source-component work, pre-existing or maintenance conditions, improvements, contents, and other-insurance or salvage effects; valuation and payment are limited to supported covered loss under the applicable form, with HO-3 dwelling replacement-cost treatment dependent on the 80-percent threshold and HO 04 90 and DP 04 95 using their stated evidence-based settlement provisions (H.6.11, H.6.21-H.6.25, H.6.31, H.7.25-H.7.29).

Water-loss claims must be escalated when claimed, incurred, or reasonably anticipated exposure exceeds $25,000, without waiting for final value, and also when source, duration, exclusion, limitation, endorsement, competing scope, shared responsibility, suspected fraud, contamination, representation, litigation, or unusual compromise issues require authority review (H.5.9-H.5.17, H.5.21-H.5.36, H.7.4-H.7.5, H.7.17-H.7.18, H.7.20-H.7.48).

Payment handling requires authority and payee checks, application of the form-specific limit and deductible, separate expense and indemnity authority, and prompt payment of supported undisputed amounts; denials or partial denials require a written explanation tied accurately to the applicable policy language (H.6.38-H.6.45, H.7.9-H.7.11). Under HO-3 2024-03, covered loss is payable within 60 days after agreement, final judgment, or filing of an appraisal award, while appraisal determines amount of loss rather than coverage or policy interpretation (S.35, S.42-S.47).

Closure requires a documented coverage decision, payment status, unresolved issues, required communications, evidence and recovery handling, and preservation of claim notes and payment records; a claim must be reopened when credible new information may affect coverage, damages, payment, or recovery rights (H.6.43-H.6.54).
